transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you, Dr. Smith. Um... I guess what finally brought me in is that I just don't really feel like myself anymore. 

I used to always make time for things I enjoyed doing. Like painting, hiking, singing in my choir... even just going to our Sunday family gatherings. But lately, even when I actually have a free hour, I just sit there. I just find myself completely unable to care about any of it.
Have you ever experienced a period like this in your life before, or is this the first time you've felt this way?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I've had times where I felt stressed or down for a few days, like anyone else. But nothing like this. This is the first time I've felt just... completely empty and disconnected for this long.
Are you currently pregnant or have you given birth within the last four weeks?
Um, no. No, I'm definitely not pregnant, and I haven't had a baby anytime recently.
How long have you been feeling this way?
I'd say it's been building for about eight months now. It started right around the time I took over the STEM-Arts curriculum initiative at work.
During this time, have you ever heard voices or seen things that others could not perceive?
No, nothing like that. I haven't heard any voices or seen anything that wasn't there.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your sleep patterns since you started feeling this way?

Yes, my sleep has been all over the place for months now. I'll just... lie awake in bed, replaying grant details in my head. Then I usually end up waking up around three or four in the morning. And honestly, even when I do manage to sleep a little longer, I still get up feeling like I never rested at all.
Have you noticed any change in how fast you move or talk, or do you feel like you are physically moving more slowly than usual?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I'm obviously exhausted from not sleeping, but I haven't noticed myself actually moving or talking any slower than normal. And I don't think I'm moving faster or anything like that, either. My movements just feel pretty average, I guess. Nobody at work has pointed anything out to me, anyway.

Looking back over your entire life, even going back to your teenage years or early adulthood, can you recall any other periods lasting at least two weeks where you felt this same deep sense of emptiness or loss of interest in things you usually enjoy?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I've had times where I was stressed or, you know, just having a bad week, but nothing like this. This feeling of just... being completely empty and not caring about anything, it's new. I haven't ever felt this way for weeks on end before.
Have you noticed any change in your appetite or your weight during these past eight months?

No, not really. My appetite has been pretty much the same as it always is. I haven't noticed any changes in my weight either. I still eat my regular meals, it's just... I guess I don't really enjoy them as much, but I'm still eating normally.
Because of these feelings, have you had to miss days of work or stop fulfilling your usual responsibilities?

Yes, I have. I've missed several teaching sessions recently, and I've been avoiding the student workshops. I just... I can't keep up with the responsibilities the way I used to. It's affecting things at home, too. My husband has had to step in a lot more because I keep withdrawing from our family plans. I just don't feel safe trying to push through it all alone right now.
Do you find yourself experiencing intense feelings of worthlessness or guilt that seem disproportionate to your situation?

Yes, I do. Um, especially with work. Whenever anything goes wrong with the curriculum project I'm involved in, even if it's just something really small, I get overwhelmed by it. I keep thinking that I'm completely letting the students down. And... I don't know, I just feel like I'm wasting all the sacrifices my parents made for me to even have this kind of opportunity. It just feels like I'm failing everyone.
